source.text: וְיוֹסֵ֖ף הוּרַ֣ד מִצְרָ֑יְמָה וַיִּקְנֵ֡הוּ פּוֹטִיפַר֩ סְרִ֨יס פַּרְעֹ֜ה שַׂ֤ר הַטַּבָּחִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִצְרִ֔י מִיַּד֙ הַיִּשְׁמְעֵאלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹרִדֻ֖הוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and bought him Potiphar, official of Pharaoh, commander of the bodyguards, a man, an Egyptian, from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.

en.L: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh, the commander of the guard, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
en.B: Meanwhile Joseph had been carried down to Egypt. The Ishmaelites who brought him there sold him to Potiphar, an Egyptian who served Pharaoh as a court officer and commanded his guard.
en.R: The Ishmaelites brought Joseph to Egypt and sold him there. The buyer was Potiphar, an Egyptian. He was an officer of Pharaoh and head of the king's guard.

es.L: Y José había sido bajado a Egipto, y lo compró Potifar, funcionario del faraón, jefe de la guardia, un hombre egipcio, de mano de los ismaelitas que lo habían bajado allá.
es.B: Mientras tanto, José había sido llevado a Egipto. Los ismaelitas que lo llevaron allí se lo vendieron a Potifar, un egipcio que servía al faraón como funcionario de la corte y era el jefe de su guardia.
es.R: Los ismaelitas llevaron a José a Egipto y allí lo vendieron. El que lo compró fue Potifar, un egipcio. Era funcionario del faraón y jefe de la guardia del rey.

fr.L: Et Joseph avait été descendu en Égypte, et Potiphar, officier du pharaon, chef des gardes, un homme égyptien, l’acheta de la main des Ismaélites qui l’y avaient fait descendre.
fr.B: Pendant ce temps, Joseph avait été emmené en Égypte. Les Ismaélites qui l’y avaient conduit le vendirent à Potiphar, un Égyptien qui servait le pharaon comme officier de la cour et commandait sa garde.
fr.R: Les Ismaélites ont emmené Joseph en Égypte et l’ont vendu là-bas. C’est Potiphar, un Égyptien, qui l’a acheté. C’était un officier du pharaon et le chef de la garde du roi.

sw.L: Basi Yusufu alikuwa ameshushwa mpaka Misri, naye Potifa, afisa wa Farao, mkuu wa walinzi, mtu Mmisri, akamnunua kutoka mkononi mwa Waishmaeli waliokuwa wamemshusha huko.
sw.B: Wakati huo Yusufu alikuwa amepelekwa Misri. Waishmaeli waliomleta huko walimwuza kwa Potifa, Mmisri aliyemtumikia Farao kama afisa wa ikulu na mkuu wa walinzi wake.
sw.R: Waishmaeli walimpeleka Yusufu Misri, wakamwuza huko. Aliyemnunua alikuwa Potifa, Mmisri. Yeye alikuwa afisa wa Farao na mkuu wa walinzi wa mfalme.

decisions.choice: Joseph had been brought down: the story returns to Joseph
decisions.reason: The sentence puts Joseph first and picks up where 37:36 left off, after the story of Judah in chapter 38. "Brought down" (hurad) echoes Jacob's words that he would "go down" to Sheol mourning his son (37:35).

decisions.choice: official ... commander of the guard: Potiphar's rank
decisions.reason: As in 37:36, saris here is a title for a royal officer, and the commander of the guard led the king's bodyguard. The narrator also stresses that he was "an Egyptian": Joseph now serves a foreign master in a foreign land.

decisions.choice: the Ishmaelites ... sold him to Potiphar
alternatives: Potiphar bought him from the Ishmaelites
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the sentence around to keep the long description of Potiphar at the end; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("acheta", "vendirent"); passé composé at Readable ("ont emmené", "l'a acheté")
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written French narrative; Readable uses the passé composé, the tense of spoken French and of school reading today. Speech keeps the tenses of speech at every level.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְהִ֖י אִ֣ישׁ מַצְלִ֑יחַ וַיְהִ֕י בְּבֵ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו הַמִּצְרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Yahweh with Joseph, and he was a man successful; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, and he became a successful man while he served in the house of the Egyptian, his master.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and made him successful. Joseph lived and worked in the home of the Egyptian who owned him.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con José, y él fue un hombre próspero; y estaba en la casa de su amo, el egipcio.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con José, y a José le fue bien en todo mientras servía en la casa de su amo egipcio.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con José y hacía que le fuera bien. José vivía y trabajaba en la casa del egipcio que era su dueño.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} fut avec Joseph, et il fut un homme qui réussissait ; et il était dans la maison de son maître, l’Égyptien.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec Joseph, et tout lui réussit tandis qu’il servait dans la maison de l’Égyptien, son maître.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec Joseph et lui donnait du succès. Joseph vivait et travaillait dans la maison de l’Égyptien à qui il appartenait.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Yusufu, naye akawa mtu wa kufanikiwa; akawa katika nyumba ya bwana wake, yule Mmisri.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Yusufu, naye akafanikiwa sana alipokuwa akitumika katika nyumba ya bwana wake, yule Mmisri.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Yusufu, akamfanikisha. Yusufu aliishi na kufanya kazi nyumbani kwa yule Mmisri aliyekuwa bwana wake.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with Joseph: the theme of the chapter
decisions.reason: The phrase frames the chapter: twice at the start (verses 2-3) and twice at the end in prison (verses 21, 23). The narrator uses the divine name here, though Joseph and the Egyptians speak only of "God". Whether in favor or in prison, Joseph is not alone.

decisions.choice: successful: things went well in his hands
decisions.reason: The word (matsliach) means one who prospers or succeeds; verse 3 says the LORD was the cause.

decisions.choice: and made him successful
alternatives: and he was a successful man
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two clauses as cause and result, as verse 3 does.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אֲדֹנָ֔יו כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא עֹשֶׂ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה מַצְלִ֥יחַ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw his master that Yahweh [was] with him, and all that he [was] doing Yahweh [was] making successful in his hand.

en.L: And his master saw that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him, and [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all that he did succeed in his hand.
en.B: His master noticed that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, and that whatever Joseph undertook, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it turn out well.
en.R: Potiphar could tell that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made all of Joseph's work succeed.

es.L: Y vio su amo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [estaba] con él, y [que] todo lo que él hacía {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo hacía prosperar en su mano.
es.B: Su amo se dio cuenta de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con él, y de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hacía salir bien todo lo que José emprendía.
es.R: Potifar veía que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con José, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hacía que todo su trabajo saliera bien.

fr.L: Et son maître vit que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [était] avec lui, et [que] tout ce qu’il faisait, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} le faisait réussir dans sa main.
fr.B: Son maître remarqua que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec lui, et que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} faisait aboutir tout ce que Joseph entreprenait.
fr.R: Potiphar voyait bien que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec Joseph, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} faisait réussir tout son travail.

sw.L: Na bwana wake akaona ya kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yu] pamoja naye, na [kwamba] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifanikisha kila alilofanya mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Bwana wake aliona kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja naye, na kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alifanikisha kila jambo Yusufu alilolishughulikia.
sw.R: Potifa aliweza kuona kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Yusufu, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliifanikisha kazi yote ya Yusufu.

decisions.choice: his master saw: even a foreigner could see it
decisions.reason: The Egyptian does not know the LORD, but he sees the results. God's blessing on Joseph is visible to outsiders, as it was to Laban with Jacob (30:27).

source.text: וַיִּמְצָ֨א יוֹסֵ֥ף חֵ֛ן בְּעֵינָ֖יו וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹת֑וֹ וַיַּפְקִדֵ֨הוּ֙ עַל־בֵּית֔וֹ וְכָל־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And found Joseph favor in his eyes, and he served him; and he appointed him over his household, and all that there was to him he gave into his hand.

en.L: And Joseph found favor in his eyes and served him; and he appointed him over his house, and all that he had he gave into his hand.
en.B: Joseph won his master's approval and waited on him personally. Then his master made him overseer of his household and handed over to him everything he possessed.
en.R: Potiphar thought highly of Joseph and made him his own servant. Then he made Joseph the manager of his home and of all his property.

es.L: Y halló José gracia ante sus ojos, y le servía; y lo puso sobre su casa, y todo lo que tenía lo entregó en su mano.
es.B: José se ganó la aprobación de su amo, y lo atendía personalmente. Después su amo lo nombró mayordomo de su casa y le confió todo lo que tenía.
es.R: Potifar apreciaba mucho a José y lo hizo su sirviente personal. Luego lo puso a cargo de su casa y de todos sus bienes.

fr.L: Et Joseph trouva grâce à ses yeux et le servit ; et il l’établit sur sa maison, et tout ce qu’il avait, il le mit dans sa main.
fr.B: Joseph gagna la faveur de son maître et fut à son service personnel. Puis son maître le nomma intendant de sa maison et lui confia tout ce qu’il possédait.
fr.R: Potiphar appréciait beaucoup Joseph et en a fait son serviteur personnel. Ensuite il l’a nommé responsable de sa maison et de tous ses biens.

sw.L: Yusufu akapata kibali machoni pake, akamtumikia; naye akamweka juu ya nyumba yake, na vyote alivyokuwa navyo akavitia mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Yusufu alipata kibali kwa bwana wake, akawa mhudumu wake binafsi. Kisha bwana wake akamfanya msimamizi wa nyumba yake, akamkabidhi kila kitu alichokuwa nacho.
sw.R: Potifa alimpenda Yusufu sana, akamfanya mtumishi wake binafsi. Kisha akamweka kuwa msimamizi wa nyumba yake na mali yake yote.

decisions.choice: served him: waited on him as a personal attendant
alternatives: worked for him as a slave
decisions.reason: The verb (sharet) is used of personal service to an important person, a higher place than general labor. Joseph is still a slave, but a trusted one.

decisions.choice: appointed him over his house: made him steward
decisions.reason: Great Egyptian households had a steward who managed the property, workers and supplies. Joseph will later have such a steward himself (43:16; 44:1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֡י מֵאָז֩ הִפְקִ֨יד אֹת֜וֹ בְּבֵית֗וֹ וְעַל֙ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית הַמִּצְרִ֖י בִּגְלַ֣ל יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֞י בִּרְכַּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ בְּכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶשׁ־ל֔וֹ בַּבַּ֖יִת וּבַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, from then he appointed him in his house and over all that there was to him, and blessed Yahweh the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph; and was the blessing of Yahweh on all that there was to him, in the house and in the field.

en.L: And from the time that he appointed him over his house and over all that he had, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.
en.B: As soon as Joseph had charge of the house and of all the Egyptian owned, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed that household on Joseph's account. Whatever the man had, at home or in the fields, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s blessing rested on it.
en.R: After that, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was good to Potiphar's household because of Joseph. Everything Potiphar owned was blessed, at home and out in the fields.

es.L: Y sucedió que, desde que lo puso sobre su casa y sobre todo lo que tenía, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo la casa del egipcio por causa de José; y la bendición {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} estuvo sobre todo lo que tenía, en la casa y en el campo.
es.B: En cuanto José quedó a cargo de la casa y de todo lo que el egipcio poseía, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo aquella casa gracias a José. Todo lo que el hombre tenía, en casa o en los campos, quedó bajo la bendición {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Desde entonces, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} trató bien a la familia de Potifar por causa de José. Todo lo que Potifar tenía fue bendecido, en la casa y también en el campo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, dès qu’il l’eut établi sur sa maison et sur tout ce qu’il avait, que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} bénit la maison de l’Égyptien à cause de Joseph ; et la bénédiction {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} fut sur tout ce qu’il avait, dans la maison et dans les champs.
fr.B: Dès que Joseph eut la charge de la maison et de tous les biens de l’Égyptien, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} bénit cette maison à cause de lui. Tout ce que possédait cet homme, à la maison comme dans les champs, reposait sous la bénédiction {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: À partir de ce moment, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait du bien à la maison de Potiphar à cause de Joseph. Tout ce que Potiphar possédait a été béni, à la maison et aussi dans les champs.

sw.L: Ikawa tangu alipomweka juu ya nyumba yake na juu ya vyote alivyokuwa navyo, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaibariki nyumba ya yule Mmisri kwa ajili ya Yusufu; na baraka ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ikawa juu ya vyote alivyokuwa navyo, nyumbani na shambani.
sw.B: Mara Yusufu alipopewa usimamizi wa nyumba na wa mali yote ya yule Mmisri, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaibariki nyumba hiyo kwa sababu ya Yusufu. Kila kitu alichokuwa nacho mtu huyo, nyumbani au mashambani, kilikuwa chini ya baraka ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Tangu wakati huo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliitendea mema nyumba ya Potifa kwa sababu ya Yusufu. Kila kitu Potifa alichokuwa nacho kilibarikiwa, nyumbani na pia mashambani.

decisions.choice: blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake: the promise to Abraham at work
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham that others would be blessed through him and his family (12:2-3). Laban was blessed because of Jacob (30:27); now an Egyptian household is blessed because of Joseph.

decisions.choice: in the house and in the field: everything he owned
decisions.reason: The pair covers all his property, indoors and out: household goods, crops and herds.

source.text: וַיַּעֲזֹ֣ב כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ֮ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵף֒ וְלֹא־יָדַ֤ע אִתּוֹ֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁר־ה֣וּא אוֹכֵ֑ל וַיְהִ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף יְפֵה־תֹ֖אַר וִיפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he left all that [was] his in the hand of Joseph, and he did not know with him anything except the food which he [was] eating. And was Joseph handsome of form and handsome of appearance.

en.L: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand, and with him [there] he did not know about anything except the food that he ate. And Joseph was handsome in form and handsome in appearance.
en.B: So the Egyptian left everything he owned in Joseph's hands. Having Joseph, he gave no thought to anything but the food he ate. Joseph had a fine figure and a handsome face.
en.R: Potiphar trusted Joseph with all his things. As long as Joseph was there, the only thing Potiphar thought about was his own meals. Joseph was good-looking, with a strong body.

es.L: Y dejó todo lo que tenía en mano de José, y teniéndolo a él no sabía de nada, salvo del pan que comía. Y José era de hermosa figura y de hermoso aspecto.
es.B: Así que el egipcio dejó todo lo que tenía en manos de José. Teniéndolo a él, no se preocupaba de nada más que de lo que comía. José tenía buena figura y un rostro hermoso.
es.R: Potifar le confió a José todas sus cosas. Mientras José estuviera allí, Potifar solo se ocupaba de sus propias comidas. José era bien parecido y de cuerpo fuerte.

fr.L: Et il laissa tout ce qu’il avait dans la main de Joseph, et avec lui, il ne savait plus rien, sinon le pain qu’il mangeait. Et Joseph était beau de taille et beau de visage.
fr.B: L’Égyptien laissa donc tout ce qu’il possédait entre les mains de Joseph. Avec Joseph, il ne se souciait plus de rien d’autre que de ce qu’il mangeait. Joseph était bien bâti et beau de visage.
fr.R: Potiphar a confié toutes ses affaires à Joseph. Tant que Joseph était là, Potiphar ne pensait plus qu’à ses repas. Joseph était beau garçon et il avait un corps robuste.

sw.L: Akaacha vyote alivyokuwa navyo mkononi mwa Yusufu, wala hakujua lolote pamoja naye, ila chakula alichokula. Naye Yusufu alikuwa mzuri wa umbo na mzuri wa sura.
sw.B: Basi yule Mmisri aliacha kila kitu alichokuwa nacho mikononi mwa Yusufu. Kwa kuwa Yusufu alikuwapo, hakujishughulisha na jambo lolote ila chakula alichokula. Yusufu alikuwa na umbo zuri na sura nzuri.
sw.R: Potifa alimwamini Yusufu na vitu vyake vyote. Wakati Yusufu alipokuwa pale, Potifa hakufikiri juu ya kitu kingine ila chakula chake tu. Yusufu alikuwa kijana mzuri, mwenye mwili wenye nguvu.

decisions.choice: he did not know anything except the food he ate: he left everything to Joseph
alternatives: he kept only his own food out of Joseph's care
decisions.reason: Most naturally the phrase means that the master no longer concerned himself with anything but his meals. Some read it as an exception: Egyptians would not eat with Hebrews (43:32), so the master's food stayed in Egyptian hands.

decisions.choice: handsome in form and appearance: like his mother
decisions.reason: The same words describe Rachel, Joseph's mother (29:17). The remark also prepares for what follows.

decisions.choice: the Egyptian / Potiphar
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וַתִּשָּׂ֧א אֵֽשֶׁת־אֲדֹנָ֛יו אֶת־עֵינֶ֖יהָ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֑ף וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שִׁכְבָ֥ה עִמִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after these things, and lifted the wife of his master her eyes to Joseph and said, lie with me.

en.L: And it happened after these things that his master's wife lifted up her eyes to Joseph and said, "Lie with me."
en.B: Some time later his master's wife set her eyes on Joseph. "Sleep with me," she said.
en.R: Later on, Potiphar's wife began to look at Joseph with desire. She told him to sleep with her.

es.L: Y sucedió después de estas cosas que la mujer de su amo alzó sus ojos hacia José y dijo: «Acuéstate conmigo».
es.B: Algún tiempo después, la esposa de su amo se fijó en José. «Acuéstate conmigo», le dijo.
es.R: Más adelante, la esposa de Potifar empezó a mirar a José con deseo. Le dijo que se acostara con ella.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après ces choses, que la femme de son maître leva ses yeux vers Joseph et dit : « Couche avec moi. »
fr.B: Quelque temps après, la femme de son maître jeta son dévolu sur Joseph. « Viens coucher avec moi », lui dit-elle.
fr.R: Plus tard, la femme de Potiphar s’est mise à regarder Joseph avec désir. Elle lui a demandé de coucher avec elle.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya mambo haya, mke wa bwana wake akainua macho yake kumwelekea Yusufu, akasema, "Lala nami."
sw.B: Muda fulani baadaye mke wa bwana wake alimtamani Yusufu. Akamwambia, "Lala nami."
sw.R: Baadaye mke wa Potifa alianza kumtazama Yusufu kwa tamaa. Akamwambia alale naye.

decisions.choice: lifted up her eyes to Joseph: looked at him with desire
decisions.reason: To lift one's eyes to someone can be simply to look; here it means to fix one's desire on him.

decisions.choice: lie with me: a two-word command
decisions.reason: In Hebrew her demand is only two words. Joseph's answer in verses 8-9 is long and careful.

source.text: וַיְמָאֵ֓ן׀וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣שֶׁת אֲדֹנָ֔יו הֵ֣ן אֲדֹנִ֔י לֹא־יָדַ֥ע אִתִּ֖י מַה־בַּבָּ֑יִת וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יֶשׁ־ל֖וֹ נָתַ֥ן בְּיָדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he refused and said to the wife of his master, behold, my master does not know with me what [is] in the house, and all that there is to him he has given into my hand.

en.L: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "Look, with me [here] my master does not know what [is] in the house, and all that he has he has put into my hand.
en.B: He refused. "You see," he said to his master's wife, "with me here, my master gives no thought to what goes on in the house. He has put everything he owns under my care.
en.R: Joseph said no. He told her, "Because I am here, my master does not need to keep track of anything in his house. Everything he has, he has handed over to me.

es.L: Pero él rehusó y dijo a la mujer de su amo: «Mira, teniéndome a mí, mi amo no sabe lo que [hay] en la casa, y todo lo que tiene lo ha puesto en mi mano.
es.B: Él se negó. «Ya ves —le dijo a la mujer de su amo—, conmigo aquí, mi amo no se preocupa de nada de lo que pasa en la casa. Todo lo que tiene lo ha dejado a mi cargo.
es.R: José le dijo que no. Le explicó: «Como yo estoy aquí, mi amo no necesita estar pendiente de nada en su casa. Todo lo que tiene me lo ha confiado a mí.

fr.L: Mais il refusa et dit à la femme de son maître : « Voici, avec moi [ici], mon maître ne sait pas ce qui [est] dans la maison, et tout ce qu’il a, il l’a mis dans ma main.
fr.B: Il refusa. « Vois-tu, dit-il à la femme de son maître, avec moi ici, mon maître ne se soucie de rien de ce qui se passe dans la maison. Il m’a confié tout ce qu’il possède.
fr.R: Joseph a dit non. Il lui a expliqué : « Comme je suis là, mon maître n’a besoin de rien surveiller dans sa maison. Il m’a confié tout ce qu’il a.

sw.L: Lakini akakataa, akamwambia mke wa bwana wake, "Tazama, pamoja nami [hapa] bwana wangu hajui kilichomo nyumbani, na vyote alivyo navyo amevitia mkononi mwangu.
sw.B: Akakataa. Akamwambia mke wa bwana wake, "Unaona, kwa kuwa niko hapa, bwana wangu hajishughulishi na lolote linalotendeka nyumbani. Amekabidhi kila kitu alicho nacho chini ya uangalizi wangu.
sw.R: Yusufu akakataa. Akamwambia, "Kwa sababu mimi niko hapa, bwana wangu hahitaji kufuatilia chochote katika nyumba yake. Kila kitu alicho nacho amenikabidhi mimi.

decisions.choice: he refused: a firm and lasting refusal
decisions.reason: The verb (ma'en) is a strong word for refusing. Joseph's answer rests first on loyalty to his master and then on God (verse 9).

source.text: אֵינֶ֨נּוּ גָד֜וֹל בַּבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּה֮ מִמֶּנִּי֒ וְלֹֽא־חָשַׂ֤ךְ מִמֶּ֨נִּי֙ מְא֔וּמָה כִּ֥י אִם־אוֹתָ֖ךְ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨יךְ אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֜ה הָרָעָ֤ה הַגְּדֹלָה֙ הַזֹּ֔את וְחָטָ֖אתִי לֵֽאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Not he [is] great in this house more than I, and not he has withheld from me anything except you, because you [are] his wife. And how will I do this great evil and sin against God?

en.L: He [is] not greater in this house than I, and he has not held back anything from me except you, because you [are] his wife. How then could I do this great evil and sin against God?"
en.B: He does not rank above me in this house. The only thing he has denied me is you, since you are his wife. How could I commit so great a wrong, and sin against God?"
en.R: In this house I have as much power as he does. The only thing he keeps back from me is you, because you are his wife. I could never do such an evil thing. It would be sinning against God."

es.L: No [es] él mayor en esta casa que yo, y no me ha negado nada sino a ti, porque tú [eres] su mujer. ¿Cómo, pues, haría yo este gran mal y pecaría contra Dios?».
es.B: En esta casa él no tiene más autoridad que yo. Lo único que no me ha permitido eres tú, porque eres su esposa. ¿Cómo podría yo cometer una maldad tan grande y pecar contra Dios?».
es.R: En esta casa yo tengo tanto poder como él. Lo único que no me ha dado eres tú, porque eres su esposa. Yo nunca podría hacer algo tan malo. Sería pecar contra Dios».

fr.L: Il n’[est] pas plus grand que moi dans cette maison, et il ne m’a rien refusé, sauf toi, parce que tu [es] sa femme. Comment donc ferais-je ce grand mal et pécherais-je contre Dieu ? »
fr.B: Il n’a pas plus d’autorité que moi dans cette maison. La seule chose qu’il m’ait refusée, c’est toi, puisque tu es sa femme. Comment pourrais-je commettre une faute aussi grave et pécher contre Dieu ? »
fr.R: Dans cette maison, j’ai autant de pouvoir que lui. La seule chose qu’il ne m’a pas donnée, c’est toi, parce que tu es sa femme. Je ne pourrais jamais faire une chose aussi mauvaise. Ce serait pécher contre Dieu. »

sw.L: Yeye si mkuu katika nyumba hii kuliko mimi, wala hakunizuilia kitu chochote ila wewe, kwa sababu wewe [ni] mke wake. Basi nawezaje kufanya uovu huu mkubwa na kumtenda Mungu dhambi?"
sw.B: Yeye hana cheo kunizidi katika nyumba hii. Kitu pekee alichoninyima ni wewe, kwa kuwa wewe ni mke wake. Ningewezaje kufanya ubaya mkubwa namna hii, nikamkosea Mungu?"
sw.R: Katika nyumba hii nina mamlaka sawa na yeye. Kitu pekee asichonipa ni wewe, kwa sababu wewe ni mke wake. Siwezi kamwe kufanya jambo baya namna hiyo. Ingekuwa ni kutenda dhambi dhidi ya Mungu."

decisions.choice: he is not greater than I: Potiphar has given Joseph equal authority
alternatives: no one is greater than I
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "he is not great ... more than I" most naturally refers to the master himself: within the house, Joseph has as much authority as he does. Only his wife is excluded.

decisions.choice: sin against God: wrong against a person is also wrong against God
decisions.reason: Joseph sees adultery as betraying his master and, above all, as sin against God (compare 20:6; Psalm 51:4). Speaking to an Egyptian, he uses the general word for God (Elohim), not the divine name.

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כְּדַבְּרָ֥הּ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֖ף י֣וֹם׀י֑וֹם וְלֹא־שָׁמַ֥ע אֵלֶ֛יהָ לִשְׁכַּ֥ב אֶצְלָ֖הּ לִהְי֥וֹת עִמָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as she spoke to Joseph day [after] day, and not he listened to her, to lie beside her, to be with her.

en.L: And it happened, though she spoke to Joseph day after day, that he did not listen to her, to lie beside her [or] to be with her.
en.B: She urged Joseph day after day, but he would not listen to her or agree to lie beside her or be in her company.
en.R: She asked Joseph again and again, every single day. But he refused to sleep with her, and he even stayed away from her.

es.L: Y sucedió que, aunque ella hablaba a José día tras día, él no la escuchaba para acostarse junto a ella [ni] para estar con ella.
es.B: Ella insistía a José día tras día, pero él no le hacía caso ni aceptaba acostarse a su lado ni estar en su compañía.
es.R: Ella se lo pedía a José una y otra vez, todos los días. Pero él se negaba a acostarse con ella, y hasta evitaba estar cerca de ella.

fr.L: Et il arriva, bien qu’elle parlât à Joseph jour après jour, qu’il ne l’écouta pas pour coucher à côté d’elle [ni] pour être avec elle.
fr.B: Elle insistait auprès de Joseph jour après jour, mais il refusait de l’écouter, de coucher à ses côtés ou même de rester en sa compagnie.
fr.R: Elle le lui a demandé encore et encore, tous les jours. Mais il a refusé de coucher avec elle, et il évitait même de se trouver près d’elle.

sw.L: Ikawa ingawa alisema na Yusufu siku baada ya siku, hakumsikiliza, kulala karibu naye [wala] kuwa pamoja naye.
sw.B: Alimsihi Yusufu siku baada ya siku, lakini hakumsikiliza, wala kukubali kulala kando yake au kuwa pamoja naye.
sw.R: Alimwomba Yusufu tena na tena, kila siku. Lakini Yusufu alikataa kulala naye, na hata aliepuka kuwa karibu naye.

decisions.choice: to be with her: even to spend time with her
decisions.reason: After "to lie beside her", "to be with her" probably goes further: Joseph avoided her company altogether.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כְּהַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א הַבַּ֖יְתָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת מְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֨ין אִ֜ישׁ מֵאַנְשֵׁ֥י הַבַּ֛יִת שָׁ֖ם בַּבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was about this day, and he went into the house to do his work, and there was not any man of the men of the house there in the house,

en.L: And it happened on a certain day, when he went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the household [were] there in the house,
en.B: But one day, as Joseph came into the house to see to his work, with none of the men of the household there inside,
en.R: On a certain day, Joseph came into the house to do his work. No other men from the household were there.

decisions.choice: about this day: on a certain day
decisions.reason: The phrase marks a particular day, one like the others until it was not.

source.text: וַתִּתְפְּשֵׂ֧הוּ בְּבִגְד֛וֹ לֵאמֹ֖ר שִׁכְבָ֣ה עִמִּ֑י וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ בְּיָדָ֔הּ וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: and she seized him by his garment, saying, lie with me. And he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside.

en.L: and she caught him by his garment, saying, "Lie with me." But he left his garment in her hand and fled and went outside.
en.B: she seized hold of his garment. "Sleep with me!" she said. But he ran from her and got outside, leaving the garment in her grip.
en.R: Then Potiphar's wife caught hold of Joseph's robe. "Sleep with me!" she said. Joseph got away and ran outside, but she was left holding his robe.

decisions.choice: his garment: Joseph loses his clothing a second time
decisions.reason: His brothers stripped him of his robe and used it to deceive their father (37:23, 31-33). Now a garment is again taken from him and used as false evidence against him.

decisions.choice: he left ... and fled: he got away at any cost
decisions.reason: Joseph does not argue or struggle; he leaves the garment behind and runs. The word "garment" (beged) is the outer clothing.

source.text: וַיְהִי֙ כִּרְאוֹתָ֔הּ כִּֽי־עָזַ֥ב בִּגְד֖וֹ בְּיָדָ֑הּ וַיָּ֖נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,

en.L: And it happened, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,
en.B: When she saw that he had run outside and left his garment in her hand,
en.R: Now his robe was in her hand, and he had run off outside.

source.text: וַתִּקְרָ֞א לְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵיתָ֗הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר רְא֗וּ הֵ֥בִיא לָ֛נוּ אִ֥ישׁ עִבְרִ֖י לְצַ֣חֶק בָּ֑נוּ בָּ֤א אֵלַי֙ לִשְׁכַּ֣ב עִמִּ֔י וָאֶקְרָ֖א בְּק֥וֹל גָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: and she called to the men of her house and said to them, saying, see, he has brought to us a man, a Hebrew, to mock us; he came to me to lie with me, and I called out with a great voice.

en.L: she called to the men of her household and spoke to them, saying, "See, he has brought us a Hebrew man to make sport of us. He came to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
en.B: she summoned the men of her household and said to them, "See here! He has brought in a Hebrew to toy with us. The man came in to me to lie with me, and I screamed at the top of my voice.
en.R: So she shouted for the men who worked in the house. "Come and see!" she told them. "My husband brought in this Hebrew, and now he treats us with no respect. He came to me wanting to sleep with me, but I yelled as loud as I could.

decisions.choice: he has brought us: she blames her husband
decisions.reason: She does not name her husband; "he" brought this man in. She turns the servants against the foreigner and against her husband's choice in one breath.

decisions.choice: a Hebrew: an outsider
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is the name others use for Abraham's family (14:13). On her lips it stresses that Joseph is a foreigner, and the Egyptians kept apart from Hebrews (43:32).

decisions.choice: to make sport of us: to mock, with a sexual edge
decisions.reason: The verb (tsachaq) means to laugh, play or make fun of; in 26:8 it describes Isaac caressing Rebekah. She means that Joseph insulted the household by making advances.

decisions.choice: My husband
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whom she means.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י כְשָׁמְע֔וֹ כִּֽי־הֲרִימֹ֥תִי קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֤ב בִּגְדוֹ֙ אֶצְלִ֔י וַיָּ֖נָס וַיֵּצֵ֥א הַחֽוּצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he heard that I raised my voice and called out, and he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside.

en.L: And it happened, when he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside."
en.B: Hearing me raise my voice and shout, he left his garment beside me and fled outside."
en.R: As soon as I started yelling, he ran out and left his robe behind with me."

decisions.choice: beside me: her story changes the facts
decisions.reason: The narrator said the garment was left "in her hand" (verses 12-13). She says it was left "beside me", as if he had undressed and run off when she screamed.

source.text: וַתַּנַּ֥ח בִּגְד֖וֹ אֶצְלָ֑הּ עַד־בּ֥וֹא אֲדֹנָ֖יו אֶל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she placed his garment beside her until came his master to his house.

en.L: And she laid his garment beside her until his master came home.
en.B: She put the garment down beside her and waited for Joseph's master to come home.
en.R: She kept the robe close by her side. Then Potiphar came home.

source.text: וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו כַּדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה לֵאמֹ֑ר בָּֽא־אֵלַ֞י הָעֶ֧בֶד הָֽעִבְרִ֛י אֲשֶׁר־הֵבֵ֥אתָ לָּ֖נוּ לְצַ֥חֶק בִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, came to me the slave, the Hebrew, whom you brought to us, to mock me.

en.L: And she spoke to him according to these words, saying, "The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us came in to me to make sport of me.
en.B: Then she repeated it all to him: "The Hebrew slave whom you brought among us came in to me, to make a plaything of me.
en.R: She repeated to him what she had said before. "The Hebrew slave you brought home," she said, "came to me to take advantage of me.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew slave whom you brought: the blame laid on her husband
decisions.reason: To the servants she said "he has brought"; to her husband she says "you brought". She calls Joseph a slave and a Hebrew, both words that set him below her.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph, who was sold and bought (37:28; 39:1); she uses the word to set him below her (m1).

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּהֲרִימִ֥י קוֹלִ֖י וָאֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּעֲזֹ֥ב בִּגְד֛וֹ אֶצְלִ֖י וַיָּ֥נָס הַחֽוּצָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, as I raised my voice and called out, and he left his garment beside me and fled outside.

en.L: And it happened, as I raised my voice and cried out, that he left his garment beside me and fled outside."
en.B: But as I raised my voice and cried out, he abandoned his garment beside me and fled outside."
en.R: I yelled, and he ran out, leaving his robe here with me."

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹנָ֜יו אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּרָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה עָ֥שָׂהּלִ֖י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when heard his master the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, according to these things did to me your slave, and burned his anger.

en.L: And it happened, when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, "Your slave did these things to me," that his anger burned.
en.B: Joseph's master listened to his wife telling him, "That is what your slave did to me," and he flew into a rage.
en.R: Potiphar listened to his wife. "Your slave did this to me," she told him. Then Potiphar was filled with rage.

decisions.choice: his anger burned: against whom is not said
decisions.reason: The text does not say whom he was angry with. He puts Joseph in prison rather than having him killed, which some take as a sign that he did not fully believe his wife.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for Joseph, who was sold and bought (37:28; 39:1); his wife's words repeat "the Hebrew slave" of verse 17.

source.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲדֹנֵ֨י יוֹסֵ֜ף אֹת֗וֹ וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֔הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אֲסִירֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲסוּרִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי־שָׁ֖ם בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And took master of Joseph him and put him into the house of the prison, the place where the prisoners of the king [were] imprisoned; and he was there in the house of the prison.

en.L: And Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison house, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the prison house.
en.B: He had Joseph taken and locked up in the prison house used for the king's prisoners, and there Joseph remained.
en.R: He had Joseph thrown into the king's prison. Joseph stayed locked up there.

decisions.choice: the prison house: a fortress or round house
decisions.reason: The word sohar is found only in Genesis 39-40. It may mean a round building or tower; here it is a royal jail for the king's prisoners, attached to the house of the commander of the guard (40:3).

decisions.choice: the king's prisoners: two spellings in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text and the marginal reading of the Masoretes spell the word for "prisoners" slightly differently. Both mean the same.

decisions.choice: where the king's prisoners were confined: a jail for royal offenders
decisions.reason: This was a prison for people who had offended the king, like the cupbearer and baker in chapter 40. That Joseph is put here and not executed is unexpected for a slave accused of such an act.

source.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶת־יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיֵּ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו חָ֑סֶד וַיִּתֵּ֣ן חִנּ֔וֹ בְּעֵינֵ֖י שַׂ֥ר בֵּית־הַסֹּֽהַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And was Yahweh with Joseph and extended to him loyalty, and gave his favor in the eyes of the commander of the house of the prison.

en.L: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and extended loyalty to him, and gave him favor in the eyes of the chief of the prison house.
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph. He treated him with loyal kindness and won him the favor of the prison warden.
en.R: Even there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and was good to him. He made the head of the prison think well of Joseph.

decisions.choice: extended loyalty (hesed): faithful kindness
decisions.reason: Hesed is the loyal love that keeps faith with someone. Joseph is a slave in prison, but God has not let go of him.

decisions.choice: the chief of the prison house: the warden
decisions.reason: The title means the officer in charge of the prison, under the commander of the guard.

decisions.choice: loyalty
decisions.reason: Literal uses "loyalty" for hesed, as in 24:12; Balanced and Readable express the warmth of the word.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֞ן שַׂ֤ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֨הַר֙ בְּיַד־יוֹסֵ֔ף אֵ֚ת כָּל־הָ֣אֲסִירִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֤ר עֹשִׂים֙ שָׁ֔ם ה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה עֹשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave the commander of the house of the prison into the hand of Joseph all the prisoners who [were] in the house of the prison; and all that they were doing there, he was the doer.

en.L: And the chief of the prison house put into Joseph's hand all the prisoners who [were] in the prison house; and whatever was done there, he was the one who did it.
en.B: The warden handed over to Joseph the care of every prisoner in the place, and Joseph directed all the work that was done there.
en.R: The head of the prison gave Joseph the job of looking after all the prisoners. Whatever work was done there, Joseph was the one doing it.

decisions.choice: he was the one who did it: everything went through him
decisions.reason: The phrase means that Joseph ordered and oversaw whatever was done in the prison.

source.text: אֵ֣ין׀שַׂ֣ר בֵּית־הַסֹּ֗הַר רֹאֶ֤ה אֶֽת־כָּל־מְא֨וּמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אִתּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲשֶׁר־ה֥וּא עֹשֶׂ֖ה יְהוָ֥ה מַצְלִֽיחַ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not the commander of the house of the prison [was] seeing anything in his hand, because Yahweh [was] with him; and what he [was] doing Yahweh [was] making successful.

en.L: The chief of the prison house paid no attention to anything in his hand, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him; and whatever he did, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made [it] succeed.
en.B: The warden never looked into anything entrusted to Joseph, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, and whatever Joseph did, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made it succeed.
en.R: The head of the prison did not bother checking Joseph's work. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was with Joseph and made all of Joseph's tasks go well.

decisions.choice: the LORD was with him: the same pattern in prison as in Potiphar's house
decisions.reason: The end of the chapter repeats its beginning (verses 2-6). Whether a trusted steward or a prisoner, Joseph prospers because the LORD is with him.
